records.text: Owens reported that Harry Myers described the man leading his interrogation as Captain Neff, about 36 years old with brown hair, and later said Neff was the commander of force protection.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And he said he was approximately 36 years old. ... He had brown hair. The one I'm talking about that was leading the charge on asking him all the questions and interrogating him and that his name was Captain Neff. ... He said that this commander, Neff, by the way, was the commander of force protection.

verification.notes: Transcript context confirms Owens relayed Myers' physical description and the name Captain Neff, later identifying that person as the force-protection commander. Current searches of Army and Fort Huachuca public material, reporting, and the incident number named elsewhere in the episode found no official roster, incident report, or independent primary record identifying a Captain Neff in that role or confirming the interrogation. Search results consist chiefly of episode transcripts and derivative speculation. The private account cannot be independently verified.

records.text: Owens said Harry Myers identified Captain Adam Neff of the 10th Mountain Division from photographs as the person who led his Fort Huachuca interrogation
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: First and foremost, I should tell you we have a positive ID on Captain Neff. He was not sure what Captain Neff's first name was. ... It was in fact Adam Neff, and I'm sure captains have different names, but Adam Neff of the 10th Mountain Division is the individual. ... I sent picture options to him as your emails were coming in, and then someone said, Adam Neff, I sent it, and he confirmed that that is the correct person. ... There were several, obviously, but Adam Neff was leading the interrogation of him. And it checks out because that is the division from New York.

verification.notes: Verification attempted. The episode says Myers selected Adam Neff from a photograph lineup, but the underlying emails, lineup, interrogation record, or an independent official account are not public. No authoritative source located confirms that Neff led the alleged interrogation. The statement now preserves the reported identification method rather than presenting the identity as independently established.

records.text: Owens cited incident-report number 8611-2025-MPC446 and said Captain Neff had given it to Harry Myers.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: It is 8611- 2025-MPC446. ... So that is the report number that was given to him by this Captain Commander Neff.

verification.notes: Exact-number searches and public Fort Huachuca searches produced no matching incident report. Owens says Myers supplied the number and suggested the report could be requested, but no report was available for authentication. The record therefore captures the attributed number while marking the underlying document unverified.
